title: Learning, memory and plasticity
stage: College neuroscience and cognitive science degree
audience: a college student in a neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology or biology degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn how experience changes behavior and the brain: classical and instrumental conditioning, the Rescorla–Wagner model, reinforcement learning and dopamine prediction errors, habits and goals, memory systems and amnesia, the hippocampus and memory consolidation, place cells and grid cells, synaptic plasticity (long-term potentiation, Hebbian and spike-timing-dependent plasticity), and associative memory networks, with models in Python.
primary_reading: Neuroscience Online, an open-access textbook from McGovern Medical School at UTHealth Houston (free)

weeks.1: Classical conditioning and the Rescorla–Wagner model
weeks.3: Reinforcement learning: values and temporal-difference errors
weeks.5: Habits, goals and the basal ganglia
weeks.8: Place cells, grid cells and cognitive maps
weeks.9: Synaptic plasticity: long-term potentiation and depression
weeks.12: Memory in development, aging and disease

blocks.deliverable: Simulate blocking and extinction with the Rescorla–Wagner rule.
Simulate temporal-difference learning on a conditioning task.
Classify supplied patient findings by memory system.
Week 7 midterm; decode position from supplied place-cell rates.
Simulate Hebbian learning with a normalizing rule.
Store and recall patterns in a small Hopfield network.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Learning model study: implement and test in plain Python a Rescorla–Wagner model and a temporal-difference model, fit their learning rates to a supplied set of trial-by-trial choices or responses, compare the fits, and write a short paper on what each model explains and what neural data would tell them apart.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
